description.narrative: This investment, which is also known as KATALIS, supports Indonesia-Australia Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (IA-CEPA) which was entered into force on 5 July 2020. KATALIS aims at a more comprehensive, high quality and mutually beneficial economic partnership between Indonesia and Australia, which covers trade in goods (including non-tariff measures, rules of origin, customs procedures, trade facilitation, sanitary and phytosanitary, technical barrier to trade), trade in services (including professional services, financial services, telecommunication services, and movement of natural persons), electronic commerce, investment, economic cooperation, competition, and legal provision.

description.narrative: Australia invested in a market entry strategy for Privy-ID, a leading digital trust provider startup in Indonesia, to enter the Australian market. Privy-ID’s mission is to create secure and user-friendly global authentication standards. It assists companies to digitise paper heavy transactions, including digital security and preventing fraudulent transactions. Australia helped de-risk Privy’s investment in the Australian market by producing a market entry strategy. This helped gain the Board’s approval to invest in Australia and Privy has now established an office in Sydney, recruited a country manager and is developing products for the Australian market. Privy has invested in becoming established in Australia and has commenced widespread marketing. One significant recent outcome by Privy is to assist in improving trade facilitation between Indonesian and Australian markets through cross border digital document signing.

description.narrative: Australia is supporting resilience in the grains value chain through two integrated initiatives. Firstly, supporting Grains Australia to provide online training programs in flour mill production and secondly delivering a grains leadership training program for Indonesian industry leaders. The online training videos on flour mill production aims to help increase the technical knowledge of flour mill workers and optimise efficiency in the handling of Australian wheat, while improving product quality and commercial returns. This will diversify demand for Australian wheat in Indonesia to help increase resilience in the supply chain, improve business to business and business to consumer links in producing innovative products using Australian flour and Indonesian spices and cocoa. The grains leadership training targets senior people in the grains industry in Indonesia with the aim of improving people to people and business to business linkages.

Australia is well-positioned to provide support to Indonesia to address skills gaps due to Australia’s highly regarded vocational system and deep connections with industry. However, there has traditionally been a lack of awareness amongst Indonesian industry around accessing Australian training opportunities. In response Katalis developed the Indonesia-Australia Skills Exchange (IASE - https://www.iaskills.org/) designed to address information asymmetry between Australian education providers and Indonesian industry and thereby facilitate business matching. The IASE also has built-in data analytics and dashboards to provide up-to-date market insights, to facilitate marketing activities, and to identify commercial skills partnerships. The IASE has grown rapidly since its launch in February 2025, with 52 Australian training providers offering a total of 338 courses. The platform also hosts 140 Indonesian businesses that were onboarded based on their interest in sourcing training from Australia. IASE represents the first (and only) platform that showcases Australian training opportunities directly to Indonesian businesses. Katalis is operating the IASE and designing a sustainability strategy so that the platform continues beyond Katalis.

description.narrative: Katalis is funding an activity to develop ed Inclusive Tourism Australia, Bali Buddies and Cross Hotels, to develop and pilot a disability accessibility application (Access Indonesia) to improve knowledge about disability-inclusive tourism in Bali. The application allows accommodation providers to conduct structured self-assessments of their disability accessibility. Providers are then able to promote their levels of accessibility on their websites. This gives an opportunity for disabled travellers to make more informed accommodation decisions when booking their holiday to Bali. The underlying application framework is being pilot tested by Katalis’s partner, Cross Hotels, a wholly Australian owned hotel provider with seven hotels in Bali. ‍ Access Indonesia is highly applicable and user friendly for both Australian and Indonesian tourism operators and disabled tourists. The application is now being socialized within the Australian and Indonesia tourism sectors. Access Indonesia is a first-of-its-kind in the region, offering a replicable model for inclusive tourism. It is also highly scalable as it can be adapted by other hotels and regions, with no IP restrictions. Some hotels in Bali have already integrated new accessibility features because of the project. It is hoped more will follow suite once awareness of the market opportunities and the application improves.

Katalis supported PT ODG Nusantara Jaya (“ODG”), one of Indonesia’s leading electrical, fire and mechanical service contractors, to establish an electrical trades training facility in Jakarta. Despite a long term skills gap, this will be the first vocational training facility for electrical tradespeople in Indonesia that can meet the high standards of the mining and manufacturing industry. Katalis funded Holmesglen Institute, an Australian state government-owned training institution, to provide six customised electrical courses for ODG and to deliver an Australian-level teacher training program known as “International Skills Training”. Initially, Holmesglen Institute had primary teaching responsibilities at the facility, with ODG’s teachers progressively taking on greater responsibility for course delivery. The facility is now delivering accredited courses allowing industrial and mining companies to source electricians who are technically competent and who have a strong foundation of theoretical knowledge and practice in electrical installation techniques and OH&S standards. Katalis’s investment was instrumental in de-risking the critical first two years of training facility establishment. The arrangement between Holmesglen and ODG, facilitated by Katalis, is commercially sustainable, and will ensure that education standards are maintained at the facility over the long term.
